data.title: bn-3o4w: official Temporal RC publisher
data.description: risk:high complete publisher range. Source-only review while public Sigil 0.35 assets build; release-tools checksum is intentionally fail-closed pending actual asset and requires a fresh exact-target vote after pinning. Review workflows/acquisition/packing/provenance/RC controls and five risk answers. No package publication approval or CAPI acceptance implied.

data.body:
[MEDIUM] The checksum-bound public Sigil identity is not preserved to the validation point. Lines 47-48 place verified bytes at the ignored, writable target/release-tools/sigil path and then run just release-dist. That recipe runs repository and Cargo-controlled checks plus component builds before scripts/release-pack.py:52-56 opens this path; the packer hashes whatever is then present and checks only that it prints sigil 0.35.0. Its final same-file hash detects mutation during packing, not substitution after acquisition. A compromised build dependency can therefore replace the validator with another binary that reports the expected version and make the candidate appear validated by the public asset when it was not. Bind the extracted binary SHA-256 into release-tools.json or another immutable workflow value and require that exact digest immediately before and after its uses, or re-extract the checksum-verified archive into a fresh isolated path after all build-controlled execution. Add a regression that replaces the destination between acquisition and pack and requires rejection.

risk:high answers:
- Failure modes: missing/wrong public checksum, wrong version, source or candidate mismatch, non-first attempt, unexpected asset, pre-existing tag/release/attestation, or immutable readback failure otherwise stop closed; the identity substitution above is the uncovered false-qualification path.
- Edge cases: main advancing, candidate attempt greater than one, exactly three ordinary assets, RC versus stable SemVer, draft-without-tag staging, attestation eventual consistency, and partial external writes were inspected. The deliberate AWAITING_PUBLIC_SIGIL_0_35_0_ASSETS value correctly stops before network.
- Rollback: before external writes, repair and produce a new first-attempt candidate after fresh review. After any draft, attestation, tag, or public release write, preserve state, burn the SemVer, and use a newly approved version; never overwrite or rerun publication.
- Monitoring: retain acquisition digest, candidate run and attempt, source/tree, three asset digests, draft/public download hashes, tag target, attestation identity, immutable-release readback, and fresh repository controls. Also compare the validator digest at every execution point to the pinned public identity.
- Validation: the 19-file persisted range, authority documents, action pins, actionlint, diff check, and focused release/acquisition tests were reviewed. Current source/debug reproduction is supporting evidence only. The public Sigil asset/checksum, first-attempt candidate, exact candidate approval, OIDC/public immutable readback, tokenless reacquisition, and CAPI caller replacement remain separate gates.

data.reason: [MEDIUM] The checksum-verified public Sigil binary is left writable across repository/Cargo-controlled checks and release-pack later accepts the path by version string instead of the archive-derived digest; see th-3tk8ws. Preserve the exact public binary identity at each validator use and add the substitution regression before re-review.

data.body: Fixed at fa7d3d8368d54d8279ed0e51f7c243d4d40fb85c: closed reviewed tool specification now pins archive and extracted executable digests. Acquisition checks the executable before exposing it; release validation checks the expected digest immediately before and finally after every invocation, including failure. Harmless mismatch fixtures require refusal before invocation; same-user concurrent isolation explicitly not claimed. Public Sigil0.35 Release34430038968 and CI34430038068 both SUCCESS, actual public archive and binary independently hashed. Full just check24Python/no-skips PASS; fresh exact-source public-binary component qualification underway separately.

[RESOLVED] Re-reviewed the full persisted range at fa7d3d8368d54d8279ed0e51f7c243d4d40fb85c. scripts/release-tools.json:1 now pins the independently measured archive and executable SHA-256 values; scripts/acquire-release-sigil.py:27-58 validates the closed spec, archive, extracted bytes, pre-execution identity, and final exposed file; scripts/release-identity.py:23-41 enforces an ordinary-file digest immediately before and finally after each call; scripts/release-pack.py:49-56,71,82,93 routes all three release-validator invocations through that helper and performs a final digest check. tests/test_release_acquire.py:86-119 and tests/test_release_identity.py:28-57 cover pre-invocation rejection and post-call mutation after both success and failure. This closes the reported substitution path within the explicitly documented exclusion for arbitrary concurrent same-user mutation.

data.reason: Fixed at exact target fa7d3d8368d54d8279ed0e51f7c243d4d40fb85c; pinned executable identity is checked before and after every release-validator call.

LGTM for persisted base 2fbb8ce88e13a0a81935d37e36764f5b7011d6aa through exact target fa7d3d8368d54d8279ed0e51f7c243d4d40fb85c, tree 9c4b8f171f00764009f597d7ec95424b13e8ad95. Reviewed all 21 changed files and direct release-path dependencies; no unresolved source-security findings. Existing thread th-3tk8ws is satisfied and resolved. risk:high failure modes: closed pins and digest checks stop missing or wrong public Sigil bytes, wrong version, validator replacement before or during a call, source drift, dirty checkout, non-first attempt, tuple or asset mismatch, existing tag/release/attestation, draft mismatch, unavailable OIDC evidence, wrong tag, non-immutable publication, or final byte mismatch; external-write failure burns the version. Edge cases: main advancement, separate first-attempt dispatch versus rerun, RC versus stable SemVer, exactly three ordinary assets, draft staging before tag creation, attestation eventual consistency, partial external writes, and the expressly excluded arbitrary concurrent same-user mutation were checked. Rollback: before external writes, preserve failure evidence and use a fresh independently reviewed first-attempt candidate; after any draft, attestation, tag, or public release write, preserve state, burn the SemVer, and publish only a new approved version without overwrite or rerun. Monitoring: retain fresh repository and immutable-owner controls, supporting archive/executable SHA-256, source commit/tree, candidate run and attempt, all three asset SHA-256 values, package/manifest/component BLAKE3, draft and public download hashes, tag target, attestation ID and closed claims, bundle/root identities, immutable readback, and web audit review. Validation: reviewed authority in notes/sigil-plugin-spec.md:2391-2580 and 3496-3517, docs/plugin-provenance-operations.md:300-327 and docs/plugin-distribution-governance.md:50-110; current Codec publisher pattern was comparison evidence only. actionlint and git diff --check passed; 12 focused benign acquisition/identity/workflow contract tests passed. The supplied full checks, supporting Sigil release runs and independent hashes are supporting evidence, not source-review substitution. Separate gates remain: lead-controlled fresh clean-clone public-binary qualification, merge to protected main, fresh control readback, successful first-attempt candidate, independent exact-tuple candidate approval, delegated publication dispatch, OIDC and immutable public readback, tokenless official reacquisition/lock/sync, real CAPI caller replacement with preserved REDs, and new stable-version promotion.
